holidays.name: National Oyster Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the briny, slippery bivalve by slurping them raw on the half shell, grilling them, or frying them up. Oyster lovers gather at raw bars to toast the humble mollusk.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food observance promoted by seafood fans and food-holiday calendars. Oysters have been eaten for thousands of years, and the day gives enthusiasts a reason to indulge.
holidays.funFact: A single oyster can filter up to 50 gallons of water a day, making oysters natural water purifiers. Oysters can also change sex during their lifetime.

holidays.name: National Waitresses and Waiters Day
holidays.description: A day for thanking the people who carry five plates at once, memorize your complicated order, and smile while you ask for extra napkins. Tip generously and be kind!
holidays.origin: An unofficial American observance created to honor restaurant servers and recognize the hard work behind the dining experience.
holidays.funFact: The word 'tip' is often (though debatedly) said to come from 'To Insure Promptness,' but this is likely a myth. The practice actually dates back to Tudor England.

holidays.name: National Work Like a Dog Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace relentless, tail-wagging productivity, or to honor the many working dogs that herd, guide, search, rescue, and sniff out trouble. Fetch those deadlines!
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that plays on the old idiom 'work like a dog' and honors the real working dogs that serve humans every day.
holidays.funFact: Dogs trained for scent detection can have up to 300 million olfactory receptors, compared to about 6 million in humans, which is why they are so good at their jobs.

holidays.name: International Beer Day (First Friday of August Observance Window)
holidays.description: Beer lovers around the world raise a glass to celebrate brewers, bartenders, and the ancient beverage itself. It's celebrated in dozens of countries with tastings, toasts, and brewery visits.
holidays.origin: Started in 2007 in Santa Cruz, California, by Jesse Avshalomov, who wanted a day to gather with friends, appreciate the people who make and serve beer, and unite the world through beer. It is observed on the first Friday of August, which sometimes lands on August 5.
holidays.funFact: Beer is one of the oldest fermented beverages in the world, with evidence of brewing going back more than 5,000 years in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt.

holidays.name: Underwear Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance dedicated to the most essential and least discussed layer of your wardrobe. Some celebrate by wearing their funkiest pair or giving the gift of fresh briefs.
holidays.origin: An unofficial novelty holiday popularized by clothing retailers and quirky calendar sites as a lighthearted excuse to talk about undergarments.
holidays.funFact: The earliest known underwear was a simple loincloth, and ancient Egyptians wore linen versions as far back as 3000 BCE.
